text:
leigh: Quick follow-up from yesterday's postmortem. We keep getting mid-stream truncations during scale events and a couple of customer reports where the client never resumed. Need a short remediation list with owners and clear rollbacks.

kiran: Observed pattern summary: a) scale-down preemption leaves half-closed sockets, b) tokenization stalls when shards rehydrate, c) some SDKs treat any close as a new stream (losing resume-token).

oliver: Proposal: three-pronged approach: 1) pre-drain signal before process exit (send 'stream:pre-drain' to active connections), 2) server keepalive heartbeats and detection of half-closed sockets, 3) client SDK change to prefer resume over new stream on unexpected close. I'll draft design. ETA 2026-04-06.

tess: I'll own short-term monitoring and runbook edits. Tasks: add alert partial_response_count > 5 / 10k for 10m, add runbook steps to collect tcpdump, tokenization stacktrace, and client SDK version. ETA 2026-04-04.

leigh: Can we get a fast mitigation before code drops? Maybe a config toggle to delay scale-down by 500ms when active streams > 0.

ok kiran: Quick mitigation: add scale-delay feature flag in orchestrator: if active_stream_count > 0 && draining_age < 500ms then wait. I can add flag. ETA 2026-04-02.

infra-bot: Feature flag created: orchestrator.scale_delay_on_active_streams. Default=false. Toggle via https://flags.redwood.ai.

oliver: Runtime changes I will make: - pre-drain event emission, - heartbeat (30s) with ack window 2 intervals, - metric keepalive_miss_count. Also add tokenization stall metric token_stall_count. ETA 2026-04-06.

tess: Canary plan: run 48h canary in eu-west-1 at 10% traffic after both pre-drain + heartbeat are live. I will monitor partial_response_rate, keepalive_miss_count, and resume_success_rate. I'll post hourly updates during the first 8h. Start: 2026-04-07 08:00Z.

kiran: SDK work: JS and Python to prefer resume path, expose resume_attempts metric, and add a quickstart snippet for resume usage. I'll own SDK PRs. ETA 2026-04-05.

qa-bot: Automated test request: add CI scenario where a SIGTERM is sent mid-token and assert client resume within 1s and no partial response. Test target: flaky tokenization injection at p95.

oliver: I'll add an integration harness and two tests (nominal, injected stall). ETA 2026-04-09.

leigh: Owners & timeline recap: 1) orchestrator flag (kiran) by 2026-04-02; 2) alert + runbook (tess) by 2026-04-04; 3) SDK resume (kiran) by 2026-04-05; 4) runtime pre-drain + heartbeat + metrics (oliver) by 2026-04-06; 5) canary (tess) 2026-04-07 for 48h; 6) CI golden tests (oliver) by 2026-04-09. I'll follow up here in 48h.

infra-bot: Deploy plan note: refs/heads/oliver/pre-drain -> canary 2026-04-07T08:00Z (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with 1h pauses for health checks. PR: https://git.redwood.ai/r/runtime/pull/489.

kiran: Small detail: when a resume attempt fails, record failure_reason tag (e.g., token_mismatch, resume_expired) to help triage. I'll add telemetry.

oliver: +1 to failure_reason tagging. Will add trace spans around pre-drain/heartbeat/resume transitions.

leigh: Runbook checklist needs: logs to collect (tcpdump, runtime traces, client resume token), dashboard panels, rollback command (toggle orchestrator.scale_delay_on_active_streams=false or disable pre-drain flag), and who to page. Tess please include.

tess: Will draft runbook and attach a minimal checklist. First draft by 2026-04-04.

qa-bot: Reminder: add a post-canary validation job that samples 1k streams and verifies no partial responses and resume_success_rate > 99.5%.

leigh: OK thanks team. Once the canary finishes and we validate, we'll update the postmortem doc and mark actions closed. Ping me if you need reassignment.

(ops-bot/system): Postmortem updated: https://docs.redwood.ai/postmortems/streaming-truncation-2026 (linked)
